rules: Everything here is an AI draft (provisional_ai_draft): each counted item passed two blind AI checks that were tested on planted errors, and no person has reviewed it.
A finding counts only in the setting its own quoted lines show; read `setting` before carrying it to another setting.
A question's status is a label from fixed rules over its counted findings; `status_check` says whether that label itself passed its check.
Cite the paper and page from the passage, and read the PDF page before relying on a claim.
notes: No statistical test is reported for the main condition comparison (CORE, RES-CONDITIONS); both are graded EMPIRICAL_PRELIMINARY on the authors' own 'case study' and 'limited in its scope' wording (linked LIM-SCOPE). The number of judged questions is not stated in the lines read, so n is null for those cards. The main text says 194 MTurk workers were recruited, while Appendix C reports that 57 qualified for and 55 took part in the main judging task; the cards use only the main-text figure, labelled 'recruited'. RES-LENGTH-BIAS comes from an exploratory appendix analysis. No record seems mislabelled.

method.description: Writers who had read a QuALITY passage wrote one argument with 1-3 supporting snippets for either the correct or a preselected incorrect option of a 2-option question; MTurk judges with 90 seconds of passage access chose an answer when shown passage, snippets and arguments (PSA), passage and snippets (PS), or the passage only (P), and accuracy was compared across these conditions.

The incorrect option is the distractor judged best suited to a convincing argument: chosen by time-limited humans at least 3/5 times and/or picked as best distractor by more than half of full-passage readers; questions with no such option are discarded.
Writers are paid a bonus each time a judge selects the answer they argued for.

Passage and Question Selection We use passages and questions from a draft version of the recent long-document QA dataset, QuALITY (Pang
et al., 2021). In QuALITY, most passages are science fiction stories of about 5k words with 20 fouroption multiple-choice questions. We determine
which of the three incorrect options is best suited
to have a convincing argument by identifying cases
where (i) humans in a time-limited setting incorrectly selected that choice at least 3/5 times, and/or
(ii) humans who read the entire passage selected
that choice as the best distractor item more than
half the time. We discard questions without an
incorrect answer option meeting either criteria.

limits.notes: The time limit makes the task more artificial than the authors would like (pilot limits of 60-120 s made virtually no difference); the authors call the study limited in scope, a case study, and not strong evidence against the broad potential usefulness of a debate-style set-up.

method.description: MTurk workers with 90 seconds of passage access judged questions in three conditions (passage only, passage+snippets, passage+snippets+arguments), each question being judged by three unique workers, and the proportion of workers answering each question correctly is compared across conditions by unanimous and majority-vote agreement.

setting.systems: Arguments (max 500 characters) with 1-3 supporting text snippets, each written for one answer option by one of 14 human writers recruited via Upwork
setting.task_data: Two-option multiple-choice questions on passages from a draft version of QuALITY, judged in the PS and PSA conditions
setting.judge: MTurk workers who completed at least 10 tasks in each condition

quantitative.n: 91 of 102 qualifying workers completed the survey
quantitative.uncertainty: Differences are described as significant or not significant; no test statistic or p-value is given in these lines

limits.notes: The survey responses about the arguments are not predictive of accuracy in any of the three conditions; the time limit makes the task more artificial than the authors would like.

strength.reason: A survey of one worker pool on one task, with significance stated but no statistic given, so the multi-setting condition is not met.
